recipes.name: Sweet Potato Cranberry Sauce Bread
ingredients_raw: 1 cup cranberry sauce, or more to taste
1 cup cooked and mashed sweet potatoes
1 cup raisins, or more to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 4 mini loaf pans.

Combine cranberry sauce, sweet potatoes, eggs, white sugar, oil, brown sugar, and vanilla extract in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer until smooth. Add flour, nutmeg, allspice, baking soda, and baking powder; mix well. Fold raisins into the batter.
Divide batter evenly among the loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes. Place loaf pans on a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Cranberry Sauce Bread
raw_recipe.description: Mashed sweet potatoes and cranberry sauce left over after Thanksgiving can be used up in this easy recipe for a moist delicious bread.

review.reviewBody: I had a little more than a cup of cranberry sauce so i matched that in sweet potatoes. I also used flax eggs instead of eggs. Mixed those first 3 together and let sit for 5 minutes. I used coconut oil instead of vegetable oil. I also cut back on the sugars and added the flour by 1/2c. increments. I think i used about 2 1/2c. of flour, which was whole wheat. I made this recipes as muffins. I filled my muffin pan and almost forgot the raisins so i added them on top and pushed them in lol! Baked at 375 for 24 minutes, they were fantastic!!

I was able to fill 6 mini loaf pans and they rose beautifully, were done exactly in 45 minutes, as the recipe said. I used 1/2 cup Stevia for white sugar and 1/2 cup dark brown sugar. Equal amounts of homemade cranberry sauce and a baked sweet potato (garnet yam). I added 1/2 c. toasted chopped walnuts. Topped the loaves with a few dried cranberries.

I had left over sweet potatoes and cranberry sauce and am so glad I stumbled across this recipe. The white and brown sugars help to offset the tartness of the cranberries and result in a beautiful mellowed flavor. But, I learned the hard way, NOT TO MAKE THIS IN A SINGLE LOAF PAN. I don't own small loaf pans so I tried to make one large oaf. The toothpick came out clean after 75 mintues but when I flipped it out of the pan the center caved in (it was not fully cooked). I tried to continue to bake and ended up over baking the ends and the middle still somewhat under backed but still edible. I may try with muffins next time, since I don't want to invest in new pans and this is a delicious way to use up those holiday leftovers.

I followed the recipe verbatim and used a single regular size loaf pan, thinking that qualified as "large" as opposed to mini loaf pans. I gave it 60 minutes and a toothpick was still coming up with fragments, then re-tried again after 70 and 75 minutes total. It was still fragmenty, and it had leavened a HECK of a lot, so at that point I just took it out. I wasn't using convection baking, so maybe that plays a factor, but it had very little structural integrity towards the top-middle part. It was super moist and fluffy but couldn't hold up like a denser bread or pound cake. Next time I'll probably divide it into two regular size pans - that would at least ensure it doesn't get as tall as it did. The finished product was very tasty! It wasn't super duper sweet, but it has a very nice moderate sweetness. The cranberry sauce didn't quite register as tart as it was when it was standing alone, so maybe if you're using a homemade or whole-berry sauce, err towards 1.5 cups or more. It toasts up wonderfully for breakfast with a sweet spread and it makes AMAZING croutons if you cut it up and crumb it. Heck, I bet it'd make amazing stuffing if you want to have a recursive Thanksgiving leftover experience.
